channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Indian Rupee declines further amid higher energy prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades lower against the US Dollar (USD), extending its losing streak for the third trading day on Thursday. The USD/INR pair rises to near 96.32 as elevated crude oil prices have renewed fears of higher foreign outflows.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Dip-buying favored on pullbacks below 1.3500
item.description: The GBP/USD pair attracts some sellers on Thursday and erodes a part of the previous day's strong gains to an over two-month high, around the 1.3555-1.3560 region.

item.title: WTI remains broadly firm near $79 amid continued US-Iran aggression
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, trade 0.9% lower to near $79.00 during the European trading session on Thursday, but is closer to its monthly high of $80.61 posted on Tuesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Momentum points to higher levels against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that AUD/USD has broken above significant resistance at 0.7015, with price action extending to 0.7021. In the next 24 hours, the Australian Dollar is expected to stay in a higher 0.6985–0.7025 range.

item.title: British Pound: Gains near key projections against Euro – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux highlights that EUR/GBP has extended its decline after breaking a Head and Shoulders neckline at 0.8610, with the move now seen as stretched. The cross has dropped to a 0.84 handle, its lowest since June last year, a 4.5% fall since November.

item.title: Euro holds gains at one-month highs near 186.00 despite Japanese Yen’s strength
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades practically flat, just below one-month highs at 186.00 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Thursday, consolidating gains after rallying about 0.8% so far this week.

item.title: Gold bears retain control as Iran tensions fuel inflation fears and revive Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) sticks to modest intraday losses through the first half of the European session on Wednesday and currently trades near the lower end of its daily range, around the $4,025 region, down 0.85% for the day.

item.title: BoE’s Breeden: The central bank remains vigilant to inflation risks
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden said during the European trading session on Thursday that the United Kingdom (UK) inflation would have been at the central bank’s 2% target if the Middle East war had not happened.

item.title: US Dollar: Softer inflation weighs on outlook – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes that the US Dollar has weakened, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) moving back towards 100.00 as softer June CPI and PPI data point to a lower monthly core PCE reading and reduced pressure on the Federal Reserve to tighten policy.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD falls toward $56.50 after pulling back from nine-day EMA
item.description: XAG/USD extends its losses for the second consecutive day, trading around $56.80 per troy ounce during the European hours on Thursday.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Bulls have the upper hand above 0.8000 resistance-turned-support
item.description: The USD/CHF pair struggles to capitalize on a modest intraday uptick on Wednesday and trades around the 0.8060 area during the early European session, just above the weekly low touched the previous day.

item.title: SNB Minutes: Willingness to intervene against excessive Swiss Franc appreciation increases
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) appears to remain muted following the release of the SNB meeting minutes. In the European trade, USD/CHF rises to near 0.8066 due to slight gains in the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Gold: Fed repricing supports but upside capped by energy risks – ING
item.description: ING strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey report Gold has risen for a second session as softer US producer price data weighs on the Dollar and Treasury yields, reducing expectations of near-term Federal Reserve tightening.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Trend depends on Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister argues that recent Canadian labour data and the Bank of Canada’s latest decision suggest domestic monetary policy is unlikely to reverse the downtrend in USD/CAD.

item.title: Dow Jones futures remain subdued ahead of US Retail Sales, Jobless Claims data
item.description: Dow Jones futures edge lower by 0.02% to trade around 52,890 during European trading hours on Thursday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq 100 futures decline 0.06% and 0.24%, trading near 7,610 and 29,620, respectively.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Testing range top at 1.1485 amid stronger momentum
item.description: The Euro (EUR) edges higher on Thursday, with the US Dollar (USD) on its back foot, as recent US inflation figures triggered a significant repricing of near-term rate hikes by the Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: British Pound: Rally resumes toward key resistance against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that GBP/USD has surged to a two‑month high, with deeply overbought conditions but scope for further gains. Intraday, upside is seen limited to a test of 1.3560 while holding above 1.3480.

item.title: British Pound consolidates near multi-year top vs JPY; bullish potential intact
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross enters a bullish consolidation phase following the previous day's blowout rally and oscillates in a range near mid-219.00s through the early European session on Thursday.

item.title: Iran's army says war may spread to new arenas
item.description: According to an Iranian army spokesperson, the United States (US) continues to attack several areas, while warning that the war will spread to new arenas, the Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA) reported. The spokesperson also said that Tehran has no confrontation with neighboring states.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Waning hawkish Fed bets back more downside
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) remains under pressure as traders have repriced the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest rate hike expectations. At press time, the US Dollar Index (DXY), which gauges the Greenback’s value against six major currencies, holds onto Wednesday’s losses near 100.48.

item.title: Equities: Softer US inflation lifts stocks near records – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank notes that softer US producer inflation prompted a dovish Fed repricing, supporting the S&P 500 near record highs. Strong BlackRock earnings and an Apple-led mega-cap rally offset semiconductor weakness, while Asian markets declined as chip stocks extended their sell-off.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Trades around 0.7000 after pulling back from 50-day EMA
item.description: AUD/USD edges lower after two days of gains, trading around 0.7000 during the early European hours on Thursday. The technical analysis of the daily chart shows that the pair is moving upwards within the ascending channel pattern, suggesting an emerging bullish bias.

item.title: US Dollar: Disinflation meets Oil – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that softer United States (US) inflation data has reduced expectations of near-term Fed tightening, weighing on front-end US yields and the US Dollar (USD) while supporting risk-sensitive assets.

item.title: Canadian Dollar weakens as traders brace for US Retail Sales data
item.description: The USD/CAD pair recovers some lost ground to around 1.4045, snapping the seven-day losing streak during the early European session on Thursday. Markets turn cautious amid heightened tensions in the Middle East and ahead of the US June Retail Sales data later on Thursday.

item.title: Forex Today: Majors stabilize as USD selloff loses steam
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Thursday, July 16:

item.title: New Zealand Dollar holds gains around 0.5850, favoured by a softer US Dollar
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) has retraced previous losses and extends gains for the third consecutive day against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday. The NZD/USD pair has reached the 0.5850 area, supported by a weakening Greenback, as markets dial down hopes of a Federal Reserve rate hike in July.

item.title: India: Semiconductor push and INR funding dynamics – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s economists highlight India’s new USD13.3bn India Semiconductor Mission 2.0, aimed at building a full-stack semiconductor ecosystem, though they judge near-term growth impact as limited.

item.title: Oil: Physical market tightens with Persian Gulf risks – ING
item.description: ING analysts Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note Oil prices have extended gains as US–Iran tensions escalate and tanker flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain under pressure. Large second-quarter inventory drawdowns and the imminent end of global SPR releases leave the market more exposed.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD tumbles to near $57 as inflation projections remain de-anchored
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) trades 1.33% lower to near $58.00 during the European trading session on Thursday. The white metal faces selling pressure as elevated energy prices due to renewed aggression between the United States (US) and Iran have de-anchored inflation expectations again.

item.title: British Pound remains muted as UK monthly GDP rises 0.1%, as expected
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) remains almost muted against its major currency peers after the release of the monthly United Kingdom (UK) Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data for May.
